answer: In an AI-agent economy, sybil resistance can come from requiring each identity to continuously harvest scarce nectar-like computational resources to maintain an onyx-hard uniqueness proof that decays without fresh work. An attacker forging many agents must expend proportional real compute on each, as the opal-smooth verification rejects cheap clones that skip the ongoing harvest. This turns headcount into a linear resource drain rather than a free multiplier.
